assignment:
Some of your friends perform community service. For example, some tutor elementary school children and others clean up litter. They think helping the community is very important. But other friends of yours think community service takes too much time away from what they need or want to do. 
Your principal is deciding whether to require all students to perform community service. 
Write a letter to your principal in which you take a position on whether students should be required to perform community service. Support your position with examples.
essay_1:
Dear Principal Morgan,

I am writing to you about if every student should have to do community service. I think you should make it required because it helps students and it helps our town to, and I think thats worth the time.

First, community service teaches you stuff you cant learn in class. Last spring my friend Danielle started tutoring second graders at Lincoln Elementary two times a week. She told me that explaining subtraction to a seven year old actually made her better at math, and she got alot more patient too. My friend Marcus joined a group that picks up trash at Riverside Park. He said he never really thought about where trash goes until he pulled like forty plastic bottles out of the creek in one afternoon. Stuff like that changes how kids think about being responsible. Alot of kids would never try something like that unless they had to.

Second, our town really needs the help. The elementary school has alot of kids who are behind in reading and the teachers cant help all of them one on one. The food bank on Main Street doesnt have enough volunteers on the weekends. If every student at our school did even a few hours a semester that would be thousands of hours of help. That would make a big difference for the people who need those places.

I know some of my friends dont like this idea. They have homework and sports and jobs and stuff they have to do for there families, and they are worried they wont have time. I get that, but I think there is a way to fix it. The rule could be small, like ten hours a semester, and kids could pick projects that work with there schedules. Some of it could even be during school, like reading to little kids during a free period. That way its a little bit for everyone but not to much for anyone.

Last, if its required then service becomes part of our school. When everybody does it its not just a few kids anymore, its something we can all be proud of together.

So thats why I hope you will make community service required for all students. A few hours from each of us can teach us things we will remember and it can help the people in our town who need it the most.

Sincerely,
Jordan Ellis
essay_2:
Dear Principal Morgan,

I am writing about whether every student should have to do community service. I think you should make it a requirement, because what students and our town get out of it is worth the hours.

First, community service teaches things you can't learn in a classroom. Last spring my friend Danielle started tutoring second graders at Lincoln Elementary two times a week. She told me that explaining subtraction to a seven year old made her understand math better herself, and she learned patience she never had before. My friend Marcus joined a group that picks up litter along Riverside Park. He said he never thought about where trash goes until he pulled forty plastic bottles out of the creek in one afternoon. Stuff like this changes how kids see responsibility, and a lot of kids would never try it if they didn't have to.

Second, our town actually needs the help. The elementary school has more kids who struggle with reading than the teachers can work with one on one. The food bank on Main Street doesn't have enough volunteers on weekends, which is a problem. If every student at our school gave even a few hours each semester, that would add up to thousands of hours. That makes a difference for the people who count on these places.

I understand why some of my friends don't like the idea. They have homework, sports, jobs, and stuff at home, and they think service will take time they don't have. That is fair, but it can be fixed with a plan that makes sense. The requirement could be small, like ten hours a semester, and students could pick projects that fit their schedules. Some of it could even happen during school, like reading to younger kids during a free period. A flexible rule would ask a little of everyone and wouldn't be too much for anyone.

Finally, a requirement makes service part of who we are as a school. When everyone does it, it stops being something only a few kids do and turns into something we all share.

So I hope you will make community service required for all students. A few hours from each of us can teach us good lessons we will keep, help the neighbors who need it most, and make our whole town a better, kinder, and happier place to live.

Sincerely,
Jordan Ellis
